tone_statements.quote: 3.2. Supra-segmental Phonemes Lairamlo has three (3) supra-segmental phonemes in the form of tones: raising, level and falling. [...] As in other Tibeto-Burman languages, Lairamlo also has three tones viz., raising, level and falling. The raising tone is marked by acute/´/ and the falling tone is marked by grave /`/ however, the level tone is unmarked. In the dialect most of the tone found in open syllables. 3.2.1.1. Raising Tone [...] kəčó 'tall' kədó 'poke' (stick) kəthú 'sour' 3.2.1.2. Level Tone [...] kəčo 'dig' kədo 'protect' kəthu 'wash' 3.2.1.3. Falling Tone [...] kəčò 'ill' kədò 'small' kəthù 'caterpillar'

sources.note: Nothing. Ch. III sec. 3.2 'Supra-segmental Phonemes' (pp. 73-75) treats only tone: three tones (raising, level, falling), minimal triplets on disyllables (kəčó 'tall' / kəčo 'dig' / kəčò 'ill'); ch. I sec. 1.4 and ch. IX repeat 'Lairamlo is a tonal dialect'. The word 'stress' does not occur in any chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent all 9 chapters + abstract + bibliography: zero hits).

tone.says: Three contrastive tones -- 'raising' (rising, marked acute), level (unmarked) and falling (marked grave) -- treated as the only supra-segmental phonemes; tones illustrated with minimal triplets on the final syllable of disyllables (kəčó 'tall' / kəčo 'dig' / kəčò 'ill'; kədó 'poke' / kədo 'protect' / kədò 'small'; kəthú 'sour' / kəthu 'wash' / kəthù 'caterpillar'); tones said to occur mostly in open syllables; no tone sandhi, downstep or grammatical tone discussed; no statement on stress anywhe…
